 Credit: Far Out / New Line Cinema The 1997 movie scene Cameron Diaz was convinced would be the death of her: “I was terrified”
 Tim Bradley November 14th, 2026 · 2:30pm GMT Follow us on Google Discover December means Christmas and loads of presents, obviously. But if you’re a Cameron Diaz fan, then you’ll also get the rare gift of a new movie, because she’s starring in a comedy called Bad Day on Netflix, which, judging by the trailer, actually looks like it might be decent. 
 Aside from Diaz, the supporting cast includes the likes of John Higgins from SNL’s Please Don’t Destroy, Backrooms and Creep star Mark Duplass and Ben Schwartz from Parks and Rec . Surely that many comedy pros wouldn’t sign up for a terrible movie, and so all things point to Diaz having something of a hit on her hands come December 11th. 
 And that’s a good thing. For a long time we didn’t get any Diaz films whatsoever because in 2014 she decided she’d had enough of the whole shebang: the travelling, the promo work, all of it. Her final film was the remake of the annoying singing ginger orphan Annie , and her performance in it was described by one reviewer as ‘overacting to the point of hysteria’, which is enough to make anyone step back for a bit, let’s be honest. 
 But few expected that break to end up stretching to 11 years, with Diaz only stepping back into acting last year with Jamie Foxx in the not very well-received, but quite well-titled, Back in Action . There was also this year’s Jonah Hill nonsense, Outcome for Apple TV, which was so self-obsessed and abysmal that we’ll pretend it never happened. 
 Instead, we’ll keep our fingers crossed for Bad Day , because when she’s on form and with a great script, Diaz is a comedy legend and has been for some 30 years now. It was clear from her debut role as a jaw-dropping blonde bombshell in Jim Carrey’s The Mask that she had much more about her than just window dressing. That was confirmed over the next couple of years as she became something of a rom-com expert; the first one arrived in 1996 with She’s the One alongside Jennifer Aniston. 
 Then the following year she signed up to go head to head with one of the most popular actors in the world, Julia Roberts, for My Best Friend’s Wedding , the heartwarming tale of a woman deciding to completely ruin her long-standing friend’s nuptials to someone else because she realises she loves him herself. Diaz played Kimmy Wallace, the bubbly, unthreatening type who is getting married to Dermot Mulroney, but it wasn’t all smooth sailing. In fact, one scene in particular was a struggle. 
 That was the scene in which the main characters have a karaoke battle in a bar, with Diaz’s Kimmy showing she is unable to sing in any way, shape or form, never an easy thing even for an actor to do. The film’s director, PJ Hogan, looked back on it with Entertainment Weekly, recalling: “We staged it as a real karaoke song, where the lyrics appear in front of you on all the monitors. So, I shot it live. Cameron just botched her way through the song, and the worse she got, the better the scene was. But then Cameron was so game that the applause started to become real.”

 In 2002, Heath Ledger turned down a $155 million movie role. Two years later, it lost a fortune and was nominated for six Razzies 
 Diaz, for her part, did not have a good time no matter how convincing the crowd’s reaction ended up being. She confessed: “I was terrified to do that scene, for real. I allowed the true terror of singing in front of people to be alive in me. I wanted to run and hide, and [co-star] Dermot Mulroney kept me there. He said, ‘You can do it, you can do it.’ In the scene, I’m just staring at him the whole time because he’s looking at me like, ‘You’re OK. You’re not gonna die.’ And I was like, ‘But I’m dying.’”
 In the end, though, Diaz’s vocal discomfort was well worth it. My Best Friend’s Wedding was a colossal success, earning $300million at the box office against a spend of less than a tenth of that amount, and was nominated for three Golden Globes. 
 Diaz would earn the first of her own four nominations two years later for the brilliant There’s Something About Mary with Ben Stiller , and let’s hope her latest effort follows more along those lines.
